facts.statement: The type locality of Invictibellatrix is the Barremian-aged Wessex Formation in the United Kingdom.
Invictibellatrix lived during the Early Cretaceous Barremian age.
Invictibellatrix is known from a single braincase discovered in the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of England.
Invictibellatrix amberina was formally described as a new genus and species by Cassius Morrison and colleagues in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Cassius Morrison and colleagues described Invictibellatrix amberina as a new genus and species

facts.statement: Invictibellatrix is estimated to have weighed between 200 and 300 kilograms and measured about 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: estimated to have a body mass between 200–300 kg and a body length of around 4 m

facts.statement: One autapomorphy of Invictibellatrix is a lightly transversely compressed skull crest with an hourglass profile.
facts.quote: The crest on the back of the skull is lightly transversely compressed and has an hourglass profile

facts.statement: A third autapomorphy is a pair of lightly curved depressions along the midline of the skull crest.
facts.quote: On the crest, distinctive, lightly curved depressions are present on the midline

facts.statement: Invictibellatrix is classified within the clade Megaraptora of the class Reptilia.
The known fossil range of Invictibellatrix is the Barremian stage, approximately 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Neurocranial characters of Invictibellatrix, such as a sub‑circular occipital condyle and a sagittal nuchal crest, support its referral to Megaraptora.
Invictibellatrix represents an early‑diverging Eurasian megaraptoran, suggesting a cosmopolitan distribution of non‑megaraptorid megaraptorans in the Early Cretaceous.
The study proposes that the absence of megaraptorans in Late Cretaceous Laurasia is best explained by regional extinction.
